title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the cote compares Sullivan-style rational models with a divided-power de Rham complex. The previous and next pages copy out Sullivan's minimal-model construction and Theorem B. This page tries to describe ordinary simplicial cochains on a simplicial set as a functor represented by a cosimplicial simplicial module. That is the integral, combinatorial analogue of Sullivan's simplicial algebra of polynomial forms, which the de Rham complex 'à puissances divisées' is meant to replace.

Ex 1. Fix n. For a simplicial set K and a k-module M, set C^n(K,M) = Hom_Sets(K_n, M) = Hom_k(k^{(K_n)}, M).
- As a functor of K this is representable. Evaluation K ↦ K_n has a right adjoint i_* (right Kan extension along the point [n] of Δ).
- By Yoneda, (i_*M)_m = Hom(Δ_m, i_*M) = Hom((Δ_m)_n, M) = M^{Hom([n],[m])}.
- Hence C^n(K,M) ≅ Hom_{Δ^}(K, i_*(M)).
- Letting n vary, the objects C^n_M := i_{n*}(M) form a cosimplicial simplicial k-module C^•_M. This gives C^•(K,M) ≅ Hom(K, C^•_M) as cosimplicial modules, so the cochain complex is obtained by 'mapping into' a universal object.
- For K = Δ_n, Yoneda identifies C^m(Δ_n, M) with M^{Hom([m],[n])}. Since the Hom-sets are finite, M^S = k^S ⊗ M; this is the last displayed formula.
- The '!' remark seems to note that C_{n,M} = i_*(M) is again a functor of M of a very simple, explicit form.

Ex 2. Normalized cochains. One considers the sub-k-modules C^{n,!}_M of cochains vanishing on degenerate simplices.
- C^{n,!}_M = ⋂ Ker(σ^*) over non-injective (surjective) σ: [n] → [m].
- This reduces first to the elementary degeneracies σ_i, i = 0, …, n−1, then to some further index set (indices i, j, illegible).
- The page ends: 'On sait que cette …', apparently recalling that the normalized cochains C^!(X_•) compute the same cohomology as the full cochains. It also seems to compare them with a de Rham-type complex Ω^*(X) or H^*(X).

Purpose: build a universal, representing cosimplicial simplicial object for (normalized) cochains. The divided-power de Rham algebra can then be compared to it simplex-wise, as Sullivan compares ∇(p,*) with cochains via integration.
errors: Index convention: the page writes M^{Hom(Δ_n,Δ_m)} for the m-th component of i_*(M) and then k^{Hom(Δ_m,Δ_n)} ⊗ M. The first is the m-simplices of the representing object; the second is cochains on Δ_n. Both are correct, but the switch of variance between the two expressions is a notational slip, not an equality of the same object.

Normalized cochains are the intersection of kernels of the maps induced by surjections [n] → [m] (precomposition with degeneracies), not of maps C^n → C^m of arbitrary σ. The partially legible formula appears to state this, with 'σ … non [injective]' as the qualifier.
Most of the page is too faint to verify the intermediate claims.

ideas.what: Cochains in degree n as a functor of the simplicial set K are representable by the right Kan extension i_*(M), with (i_*M)_m = M^{Hom([n],[m])}. Together these form a cosimplicial simplicial module C^•_M with C^•(K,M) ≅ Hom(K, C^•_M).
ideas.modern_name: Representing cosimplicial simplicial module for cochains (coskeletal / right Kan extension description; simplicial cochain algebra C^*(Δ^•))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; implicit in Eilenberg–MacLane and Kan; used systematically by Sullivan (1977) and Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976) for PL forms vs cochains

ideas.what: Normalized cochains as the intersection of kernels of degeneracy maps.

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard working notes reformulating simplicial cochains as maps into a universal cosimplicial simplicial module, together with the normalization. This is classical material serving as background for comparing a divided-power de Rham complex with Sullivan's polynomial forms. Nothing beyond routine was decipherable.
transcription_corrections: Last display: M ↦ C^n_{•M} = i_*(M) = ([m] ↦ M^{Hom(Δ_n,Δ_m)}); the right-hand k^{Hom(Δ_m,Δ_n)} ⊗ M refers to cochains on Δ_n.
In Ex 2 the index under ⋂ reads Δ_n → Δ_m with σ 'non injective' (degeneracies), followed by reductions to elementary degeneracies indexed by i and by i, j.
Final line likely reads 'C^!(X_•) … H^*(X)' or 'Ω^*(X)'; illegible.
